hypothesis: The exact-sum GPU matrix-product component meets the design budgets on the host builds, checks and time model.
prediction: Budgets (baseline -> target): output bytes differing from the CPU kernel, no GPU path -> 0 with checksums and text equal to the host reference; copies per weight, code and sum byte, 1 weight expansion per call -> 0,0,0; jobs per recording, not possible (3,968-byte output, 31 workgroups) -> 204, one per call; USC instructions per MAC at most 1.75 and code at most 4,000 bytes; temps per instance at most 112 (keeps 8 tasks resident); GPU compute all channels, 14.894 s on the A55 -> 0.574 s issue-bound (0.72 s or 0.90 s if an instruction assumption fails; 1.66 s with 200-clock loads); DRAM bytes read per MAC 0.75 per lane, 0.156 per workgroup with cache reuse; lines maintained on core 6 per recording GPU only 597,601 cleaned and 988,060 cleaned and invalidated tags included; DSB SY per job 6 from three helper calls; tag words per recording 815,008; read-out instructions per recording at most 43.3 M (3 per int32 output, 4 per int64, 1 more per residual output; 155 M scalar); checks per job at most 12 compares, no translation, no hash; ring and record bytes per job at most 300 (baseline bound 368); linear stage best channel split on the A76 pair 14.894 s -> 0.629 s with 90% of MACs on the GPU at 494 MHz and 0.396 s with 63% at 2,002 MHz; linear stage GPU only 0.677 s at 494 MHz and 0.612 s at 2,002 MHz; GPU leaf entries 17 (fifteen 2 MiB pages, two 4 KiB) against 4 KiB-only at most 256 table pages; no .text growth in images that link pvr_compute_job.c (base 147,712 to 290,272 bytes per image). Time-model assumptions: USC one 32-lane instruction per clock at 400 MHz at 1.75 instructions per MAC; each task waits L clocks after each of 12 loads per pass of 4 K steps and 32 sum stores with R=8 resident tasks at 106 temps; per job firmware 25 us, submit to kick 25 us, completion to wake 25 us; cache line 20 cycles, hand-off to core 7 10 us; A76 twice an A55's NEON MACs per clock. Instruction mix: 4x4 tile over 4 K steps is 64 multiply-adds, 12 word loads, 32 signed extractions and about 4 loop instructions (1.75 per MAC); two-instruction extraction 2.19 per MAC (0.72 s); half-rate multiply-add 2.75 (0.90 s). Latency: above 112 temps fewer than 8 tasks fit; with 8 tasks a pass is latency-bound above about 127 clocks. Bandwidth: without reuse 12 bytes per 16 MACs, 3.1 GB per recording, 5.5 GB/s; with reuse 80 bytes per 512 MACs, 0.65 GB. A second job in flight: 0.629 s -> 0.593 s (5.8%) at 494 MHz and 0.396 s -> 0.394 s (0.6%) at 2,002 MHz on the A76 pair; no gain on the A55 pair (0.813 s against 0.812 s). Left-out changes at 2,002 MHz: read-out of the GPU share on both cores 0.3% (2.8% at 494 MHz), larger CPU-channel share on core 7 0.1%, producers cleaning their own code lines at most half of the 6.0 ms serial clean (0.8%), one maintenance pass per submit at most two DSB SY per job, 408 per recording, under 0.1% at 1 us each. A76 pair alone 3.72 s at 494 MHz and 0.918 s at 2,002 MHz; dispatcher goal 0.15 s. Dispatcher placement tool counts 12 read-out instructions per sum and gives 0.414 s on the A76 pair at 2,002 MHz; this model counts 3 to 5 and gives 0.396 s.

conditions.builds: each commit exported with git archive, shared configuration script, -DSUNSTONE_GPU_COMPUTE_APPLICATION=ON, -j 6 under ~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/gpu-mimus-compute-measure/r3/; seven targets that compile drivers/gpu/pvr_compute_job.c (GPU, compute, free-list, IRQ, memory and power service models, GPU render application); llvm-size -A

conclusion: Budgets are met except those tied to the instruction count: 3.39 groups per MAC against 1.75, 7,624 code bytes against 4,000, GPU compute, the three linear-stage times and one extra GPU leaf entry. The slower GPU program moves channels back to the CPU; at 2,002 MHz the linear stage takes at least 0.535 s against 0.396 s and misses the 0.4435 s pipeline goal. All left-out changes stay below the 2% rule at every latency tested. No USC instruction has been executed; board items remain.
narrative: Host-only measurement. Method: unchanged job bytes -- at both commits apps/gpu-program/compile.py compiled the affine and vector-addition programs for profile two and the transpose and neighbor programs for profile three, and checks/pvr-compute-package.py compared native PDS and CDM bytes with the pinned Mesa generators; checks/pvr-compute-service.py ran its first three emulator cases; checks/pvr-compute-job.py compared the fixed job with Mesa's reference (at the base the reference build stops at the missing header pvr_ccb.h). New checks gpu-mimus-program.py, gpu-mimus-layers.py and gpu-mimus-readout.py ran; gpu-mimus-time-model.py ran twice (design assumptions, then measured call list, groups per MAC, temps and read-out counts) printing issue-bound times and times for load/store latencies of 50, 100, 200 and 400 GPU clocks. The base has no GPU path, so its rows are the CPU profile in docs/mimus.md or the design baseline. Results (metric: result): output bytes differing 0 of 12,923,134 bench outputs and 0 in every other case; copies 0,0,0; jobs 204; groups per MAC 3.39 (217 per 64 MACs); code 7,624 bytes in two 4 KiB program pages; temps 106; GPU compute at least 1.111 s issue-bound, 1.726 s with 200-clock loads; DRAM bytes per MAC per lane 0.75; lines 597,397 cleaned (204 below the design because the model aligns every call's codes to 64 bytes and the design counts one extra line per job) and 988,060 cleaned and invalidated; DSB SY per job 6; tag words 815,008; read-out 37.6 M instructions (bias in every layer); compares per job 9, no translations, no hashes; 276 bytes per job (184 ring, 92 job-word); best split 494 MHz at least 0.997 s with 80.6% on the GPU, 1.328 s with 71.5% at 200-clock loads; best split 2,002 MHz at least 0.535 s with 45.5%, 0.664 s with 33.5% at 200-clock loads; GPU only 2,002 MHz at least 1.149 s, 1.764 s with 200-clock loads; leaf entries 18. Inner-loop groups per 4 K steps of one lane: 64 imadd32, 32 ibfe, 32 selects the compiler adds after each extraction for a zero field width, 42 register moves, 36 for 64-bit address adds, loads and load waits (add64_32, ld, wdf), 11 loop control. The pinned compiler translates every signed field extraction (including two shifts) as ibfe plus a select on the field width even for constant width 8 or 16. Four rewrites rejected: extraction with mul_hi and pointers incremented per load stream both added moves, a separate per-row product sum added multiply-adds, a 64-bit accumulator did not compile within two minutes; keeping the 64-bit base of each load stream in a register cut each address computation from two groups to one and is the shortest loop found. Two reductions need board evidence: 16-byte loads (four words per instruction once alignment is shown) and run-time shift amounts (a first attempt put shift amounts in scratch memory, which the profile forbids). Latency: the pinned scheduler places a wdf wait after each load, so a lane's 12 loads per pass complete one after another and its 32 sum stores (4 rows x 4 channels x 2 words) each follow idf and wdf; 106 temps allocate in units of 8 so a 32-lane task holds 32x112 registers; unified store 28,672 temps (256 rows x 8 banks per instance less two reserved 128-register lines, 16 parallel instances) holds 8 tasks. Model charges max(issue, chain/R) clocks per task: issue 217 groups per pass, chain 217+12L per pass plus 32L for stores, R = 8 or the workgroup count if smaller. Table by L (all channels; best split 494 MHz; best split 2,002 MHz): issue-bound 1.111 s; 0.997 s 80.6%; 0.535 s 45.5% / L=50 1.111 s; 0.997 s 80.6%; 0.535 s 45.5% / L=100 1.111 s; 0.997 s 80.6%; 0.540 s 45.1% / L=200 1.726 s; 1.328 s 71.5%; 0.664 s 33.5% / L=400 3.313 s; 1.890 s 53.5%; 0.814 s 18.4%. At 100 clocks only jobs of fewer than 8 workgroups change; at 2,002 MHz n_gpu for the 176x176 shapes falls from 80 at 100 clocks to 64 at 200 and 32 at 400. 200 clocks is 500 ns at 400 MHz; no measurement of the A733 GPU load latency exists. Left-out savings with measured constants at 2,002 MHz on the A76 pair, issue-bound: second job in flight 0.33%, read-out of the GPU share on both cores 0.02%, larger CPU-channel share on core 7 0.00%; with 400-clock loads -0.70%, -0.14% and 0.53% (a second job halves each job and small jobs keep fewer tasks resident); all below the 2% rule. Images (.text base -> change; .rodata base -> change): GPU service model 148,480 -> 148,480; 135,416 -> 135,416. Compute service model 184,440 -> 183,928; 137,684 -> 137,684. Free-list service model 151,504 -> 151,504; 135,362 -> 135,362. IRQ model 147,712 -> 147,712; 135,304 -> 135,304. Memory model 153,776 -> 153,776; 135,432 -> 135,432. Power service model 153,680 -> 153,680; 136,244 -> 136,244. GPU render application 290,268 -> 289,968; 150,768 -> 150,848. .data and .bss equal in every image. Compute service model .text 512 B smaller; render application .text 300 B smaller and .rodata 80 B larger (220 B smaller in total). The profile-three PDS and CDM encoders, fence program and firmware command are external functions shared with the mimus session; the job builder inlines all four and the linker drops the external copies because no image links the mimus session yet; before linking pvr_compute_job.c's object is 21,148 bytes against 20,120 in the service models and 11,672 against 10,820 in the render application. The two grid encoders are always_inline since the render application's options otherwise keep them out of line; the word-copy loop is not unrolled so constant PDS tables stay in .rodata. image keeps noinline: without it pvr_compute_job.o grows by 2,644 bytes; with noinline on the four encoders the IRQ model .text grew 256 bytes (28 bytes of call overhead rounded by section alignment) and the render application 324. Review responses: the model uses 8 resident tasks from Mesa's formula (a reviewer suggested about two); the single-load latency probe settles it. Package and service checks: at both commits every package check and service case passed; the 12 packages (six per profile) and their four programs are byte-identical; the open path made no timed waits; yield counts of the first two cases were 6 and 5 at the base and 5 and 6 at the change (varies between 5 and 6 per emulator run at the same commit); both 267,368-byte fixed jobs equal Mesa's reference at the change (probe.c, probe.h and probe.spv copied from an earlier check run). Raw outputs: ~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/gpu-mimus-compute-measure/r3/ (images.txt, evidence/program, layers with calls.txt, readout, package-{base,head}-p{2,3}, service-{base,head}, jobcheck-{base,head}, time-model-design.txt, time-model-measured.txt).

hypothesis: The exact-sum kernel produces bit-identical recognition output on the board with a sound cache contract and the modeled GPU timing.
prediction: Board evidence that would confirm the design: the bench recording's 204 jobs give output bytes identical to the CPU kernel and no tag mismatch while cores 6 and 7 rewrite activations at the same addresses (per-job GPU cache contract and cross-core clean); after boot the tag area reads zero and DC CIVAC at EL1 on the read-only output region completes without a fault; from timeline timestamps, GPU time per layer shape (instructions per MAC, multiply-add rate, bandwidth) against a single-load latency probe, firmware latency per job, and a job streaming 30 MiB through 2 MiB pages against one streaming 2 MiB (TLB-miss cost); on an A76 at each admitted clock, nanoseconds per cleaned and invalidated line, per read-out output and per ParallelFor hand-off; CPU and GPU branch times per shape to set n_gpu; SPI 63 delivery for every job with submit-to-kick plus completion-to-wake under 50 us; a GPU store through a read-only mapping faults, a load or store into a gap ends in RESET, and the session's ranges use planned GPU page sizes. A job with a lane removed from the grid reports a missing tag (docs/gpu-mimus.md). Until INTID 95 delivery is qualified the 4 ms timed wake adds up to 0.82 s over 204 jobs.
conclusion: Not yet run for recognition-sized workloads. Two exact-sum shapes (K=512 and K=516, 33 rows by 17 channels, 1008 MHz, 960 mV, port 3-1, 2026-10-28) passed through the returning caller; see docs/gpu-mimus.md.
